newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet near midday Monday, with light bids at $67.00 per cwt passed by owners pricing cattle $69.00 to $70.00, feedlot sources said. There were no reported trades.
Packers were not expected to start buying cattle again until Wednesday following last week's active sales, which supplied more than adequate live inventories, they said.

Last week's sales in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area were 101,600 head and movement in Kansas totaled 98,800, USDA statistics showed. The active trading also helped keep most feedlots current in their marketings, they said.
Most of last week's cattle sold at $69.00 on Tuesday, with light sales reported at $68.00 late into the week.
The sales were $1.00 to $2.00 higher than the previous week, with gains attributed to strength in the beef market, the feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle sales this week were seen at $68.00 amid concern that beef prices had topped and that the brisk retail demand that had driven prices higher was slowing, they said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.12 to $0.23 per cwt, with 47 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
